result.notes:
Commit bc3013c on branch partura-steering in /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube-steering. No existing WP8 commit was found at start (git log -40 showed WP1-WP7(+fix)/WP9(+fix) done, WP8/10/11 not).

New public surface introduced (for reviewers and later packages):
- pipeline.run_mining(..., daily_root: Optional[Union[str, Path]] = None, ...) — placed right after mirror_root, forwarded into open_cube_store. One say() line now reports whether a daily store is attached: "daily fields <dir>: <fields resolved>" (derived+log+stored, via dailyfields.available) or "daily fields: none attached" — fires unconditionally (both branches), since the design's "so a run log shows whether the data was found" reads as covering both outcomes; trivial to make it fire only on the attached case if a reviewer prefers silence otherwise.
- research.evaluate_factors(..., daily_root=None, ...) and calculate.run_factor_calculation(..., daily_root=None, ...) — same keyword, each forwarded to their own store construction (CubeStore(...) / open_cube_store(...) respectively), placed right after max_symbols.
- mining.env.BatchRewarder(..., accept: Optional[Callable[[Expression], bool]] = None, ...) — new attribute self.accept, new counter self.refused_accept, new RewardResult.reason string "rejected by accept hook" (distinct from "banned substructure"). Implemented as ONE `if (banned) or (hook rejects):` exactly as the design's snippet shows, branching only inside for which counter/reason to use; a banned structure short-circuits before the hook is ever called (pinned by a test with a hook that raises if invoked).
- pipeline.run_mining's RL branch now: (a) forwards dates=list(view.dates), warmup=trim into make_scorer, matching what gp.py already does for GP; (b) validates every banned_substructures key with mining.gp.check_ban_key(key, reg, reg.fields) before constructing BatchRewarder — previously only the GP path validated, so a malformed --ban key silently banned nothing on an RL run; (c) forwards cfg.get("hooks").accept into BatchRewarder(accept=...), None when no "hooks" key is present (byte-identical to omitting it).
- cli.py: --daily-fields DIR and repeatable --plugin MODULE on the shared `common` parser (research/calculate/mine all take them); --wall-seconds SECONDS on `mine` only. main() now collects plugin names from --plugin (if any) else $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS (not merged) and calls plugins.load_plugins(names) before args.fn(args), printing "plugins: ...". --fitness lost its static choices=; cmd_mine now does `if a.fitness not in scorer_kinds(): raise SystemExit(...)` as the very first thing (before touching --store), after plugins have already loaded, so a plugin-registered kind validates correctly. cmd_mine also fills gp["hooks"] = search_hooks_from(a.plugin) when non-None and always sets gp["wall_seconds"] = a.wall_seconds (0.0 default, matching GPMiner's own default so this is inert unless passed).
- pipeline.run_mining's run meta.json gains a new "store_contract_hash" key (getattr(store, "contract_hash", None)) — not previously recorded at all; required by the design's own test-plan wording ("the run meta records the daily-aware contract_hash"). Confirmed via grep that no existing test asserts an exact key set on this meta.json, and the full suite stayed green.
- Defensive addition beyond the literal steps list: `gp.pop("warmup", None)` in the GP branch right before passing `warmup=trim` explicitly into GPMiner — nothing sets gp_params["warmup"] today, but the design's own "the caller cannot know trim" reasoning implies pipeline must own that value, and without the pop a future caller setting it would hit "got multiple values for keyword argument 'warmup'".

Points I'm not fully certain about (flagging for review):
- The design's "Store wiring" prose and WP8's own step 9 both say "calculate.py:95 and :209 both call open_cube_store" under run_factor_calculation's banner, but in the current source those are two DIFFERENT top-level functions: run_factor_calculation (now threaded with daily_root) and export_run_to_parquet (left untouched). I did not add daily_root to export_run_to_parquet because: it never evaluates a daily leaf (only reads store.view()/read_status() for lifecycle masking of ALREADY-computed factor values), WP8's CLI-threading step 13 names only cmd_research/cmd_calculate -> run_factor_calculation, and cmd_calculate's own --parquet call already doesn't pass daily_root today. Treating this as the design doc being imprecise about which function owns which line, not as a second keyword to add — but flagging in case the intent was broader.
- cmd_mine's `search_hooks_from(a.plugin)` call (per the design's literal text) only consults the --plugin list from THIS invocation, not main()'s env-var fallback. So a module loaded only via $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS gets its operators/scorer kinds registered (through main()'s load_plugins) but NOT its search_hooks() picked up by cmd_mine unless also passed via --plugin. Implemented exactly as specified; noting it as a possible surprise for a sweep script that relies solely on the env var.

Files touched outside WP8's owned list (documented per the task's deviation protocol): tests/test_production.py, one assertion in test_cli_mine_takes_the_fitness_and_smoothing_knobs. That test asserted parser.parse_args(["mine", ..., "--fitness", "sharpe"]) itself raises SystemExit -- exactly the old choices= behaviour design item (c) deliberately removes ("A typo is now rejected by cmd_mine with a different message instead of by argparse"). Minimal fix: parse the args (now succeeds) and assert cmd_mine(args) raises SystemExit instead. No other line changed in that file.

New test file tests/test_cli_daily_and_plugin.py (19 tests) covers every bullet in WP8's own test list plus argparse-level pins (--wall-seconds/--plugin/--daily-fields/--fitness-no-choices), main()'s plugin-collection precedence (--plugin over $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS, and getattr's fallback for `synth` which has no --plugin attribute at all), library-level daily_root pins for evaluate_factors/run_factor_calculation (not only through the CLI), and a precedence test for BatchRewarder's combined banned/accept check (banned short-circuits before the hook is consulted). Did one live falsification check (temporarily disabled the new check_ban_key validation call, confirmed the relevant test fails with "DID NOT RAISE", restored) to confirm the suite isn't passing vacuously.

Style: Chinese comments in pipeline.py/mining/env.py match those files' existing predominant style; cli.py help text additions are English, matching the more detailed existing help strings there (the file already mixes both). Type annotations mirror the exact existing patterns (Optional[Union[str, Path]] for daily_root, matching mirror_root's own annotation; Optional[Callable[[Expression], bool]] for accept, matching plugins.SearchHooks.accept's own annotation). No __all__ list needed updating anywhere -- every change is a new keyword/attribute on an already-exported name, not a new top-level name.
deviations: tests/test_production.py (outside WP8's owned-files list; minimal one-assertion fix, documented inline in the diff): test_cli_mine_takes_the_fitness_and_smoothing_knobs asserted that argparse's parse_args() itself raises SystemExit for an unrecognized --fitness value. That is exactly the pre-WP8 choices= behaviour the design explicitly retires (deliberate behaviour change (c): '--fitness loses its argparse choices=... rejected by cmd_mine... instead of by argparse'). Changed the assertion to parse the args (which now succeeds) and then expect cmd_mine(args) to raise SystemExit instead; no other part of that test or file touched.

calculate.py: daily_root was threaded only into run_factor_calculation's own open_cube_store call, not into the separate export_run_to_parquet function (which the design's prose attributes the same 'calculate.py:95 and :209' line pair to, together with run_factor_calculation). export_run_to_parquet never evaluates a daily leaf -- it only reads store.view()/read_status() for lifecycle masking of values run_factor_calculation already computed -- and WP8's own CLI-threading step and cmd_calculate's --parquet call site both leave it alone, so I read the design's line-pair reference as imprecise about which function owns which call rather than as a second keyword to add. Flagged for review in notes.

pipeline.py GP branch: added `gp.pop("warmup", None)` right before passing `warmup=trim` explicitly into GPMiner -- not a numbered step in the design's steps list, but a direct, minimal consequence of its own stated reasoning ('the caller cannot know trim'), added defensively since nothing today sets gp_params['warmup'] but doing so would otherwise crash with a duplicate-keyword TypeError.
